prospect.name: Felipe Dublanc
prospect.location: Deep countryside, Devon, United Kingdom — recently relocated from London
prospect.occupation: Architect. Ten years in a family design and architecture business; currently changing direction and about to build a sauna prototype to commercialise in Devon. Work is mainly sedentary at a computer, though the last two to three months have been physical house renovation work.
prospect.family_status: Married; wife does the home cooking. Two daughters aged six and three.
prospect.training_background: Consistently active. Trained at a London gym three to four times a week until about a year ago, including a weekly kettlebell class, then took up boxing. Played squash competitively in a first-division local league when younger, stopped for fifteen years after the Achilles rupture, and recently returned at close to his former level. Follows Trevor's free Instagram mobility work after squash. Has done almost no training for the last three months because of the house renovation.
prospect.medical: Ruptured his right Achilles tendon roughly fifteen years ago and had THREE operations on it — the wound became infected, required repeat surgery, and on the third occasion was left open to dry from the inside. He retains permanently reduced dorsiflexion in the right ankle: 'I don't have full mobility on my right ankle. It's a bit stiff... it just doesn't bend as much as the other one.' He regards it as permanent — 'that's something I have to leave with'. Separately, a more recent muscle tear in the shoulder sustained playing squash, treated with physiotherapy, which he reports as currently settled. No other limitations, no lower back or hip stiffness. No health conditions were asked about, so none are recorded.

signals: Lost ground to a specific hard season rather than to neglect — a house move out of London and a full renovation of a 1930s five-bedroom property: 'the last three months, I've been mainly doing house renovations, so I haven't done much sport, and I feel I need to pick it up'
Wants a recent former self back and dates it precisely: 'A year ago it was quite in shape', now self-describes as 'skinny fat' and 'things are feeling a little bit loose at the minute'
Mild regret rather than the heavy kind — 'getting rusty and softy'

Competing reading worth flagging for the rollup: he could be scored the_optimizer on profile (46, active, plays competitive squash, wants to 'chisel it a bit more'), but he fails that avatar's defining test because price was a hard barrier, not a quality signal — 'I'm not sure I can fit nearly $1,000 a month on fitness'. The confidence is set at 0.6 to reflect that genuine ambiguity.

goals.text: Define his body more and put on some muscle, particularly across the shoulders
Lose the 'spare tire' — 'It's not too big, but it's just not tight enough'
A structured programme he can do at home, since the move to deep countryside left him with no gym nearby
More energy for his two young daughters — 'I don't have enough energy to dedicate to them after all I do'
Still be physically capable with his children decades from now, prompted by the rep's story about a 63-year-old hiking guide
Avoid further injury and protect the Achilles and shoulder in the long term

pains.text: Three months with almost no training after the house move and renovation — 'getting rusty and softy'
No gyms near the new home in deep countryside Devon, so the old routine is simply unavailable
Permanently restricted right ankle after a ruptured Achilles and three operations
Recent shoulder muscle tear from squash requiring physiotherapy
Sleeping roughly five to six hours — in bed at 11 or 12, awake at 6 with young children
Not enough energy left for his daughters at the end of the day
Cash is fully committed to the renovation — 'we're sort of breaking even almost, if you like. I'm just putting everything into the house'
Regular beer intake, several at weekends plus midweek depending on the week

objections.raw_quote: Okay. I will need to... Yeah. ... To think about it, I think it's a lot more than what I was expecting. So it's 1,000 pounds a month, basically
objections.rep_response: Asked what number he had in mind, which surfaced the gym-membership expectation, then isolated: 'apart from the finances, do you feel good about it? Is there anything else that would be stopping you from being 100% in?'

objections.raw_quote: It's just at the minute, as I said, I'm doing up a house and finances, budget is a little limited... I'm having a lot of outgoings with the renovations, so I'm not sure I can fit nearly $1,000 a month on fitness, to totally honest.
objections.rep_response: Gave the upfront norm ('most of the guys just put it on credit card and put it up front'), reassured him about not being put in a rough spot, then offered custom payment structuring: 'we don't have any... Everything like a set in stone. Everything is done custom.' Then ran a financial-picture sequence: monthly surplus, savings, and investments including crypto.

objections.raw_quote: I think in two months. Past half of it, yeah.
objections.rep_response: The rep asked the question that produced this — 'what's your timeframe on doing this renovation? When do you feel it's the more, when you will have more breathing room in terms of finances?' — confirmed 'So after summer?' and then did not address it at all. No timing play was run and no deferred start was offered.

objections.raw_quote: Okay. Then can we, let me think about it, do a bit of numbers and I'll drop you an email.
objections.rep_response: Pushed back once, effectively: 'We can talk right now and you will know because I also have like a limit that I can do and what I cannot do.' That worked and reopened the money conversation. When the prospect repeated it four minutes later — 'I'll do a bit of numbers, and I'll drop an email and see' — the rep conceded and booked a follow-up.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Sketched, not agreed: 'if you say, like, you have, I don't know, in savings, you have $3,000. So, okay. And then the rest we could... you could put down the 3K, and then we could split the rest in some installments.' No instalment count, no schedule, no total and no interest position were stated. The $3,000 figure was the rep's hypothetical, not a number the prospect gave. The twelve-month tier was never mentioned. A GBP conversion was attempted and the transcript renders it too poorly to reconstruct — the prospect said 'it's 1,000 pounds a month, basically' and the rep replied 'A pound, it's going to be 4 and 1 half'.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Asserted twice with no terms whatsoever: 'Trevor's going to be working like for six months. That's the full transformation. That's a guarantee on that' and 'the idea of working with Trevor, why is it six months? First of all, that's the amount of time he needs to get through the full transformation, and also there's a guarantee on this.' Unlike other calls in this corpus, the eight-kilogram strength condition was never stated.

prospect_financials.note: He would not give a number and the rep pressed twice. Monthly surplus: 'At the minute, as I said, we're sort of, yeah, breaking even almost, if you like. I'm just putting everything into the house.' Holds investments including cryptocurrency, currently down in value — 'we put a bit into investments and things like this'. Credit cards and available credit were never asked about. The $3,000 savings figure in the payment discussion was the rep's hypothetical.

evidence: No payment, no link, no agreement to any structure
Prospect twice deferred to doing his own arithmetic — 'let me think about it, do a bit of numbers and I'll drop you an email' and 'I'll do a bit of numbers, and I'll drop an email and see'
Follow-up booked live for Friday 7:30pm UK time on the same link, moved from 6pm at the prospect's request because he collects his children from school at five

Counter-evidence toward a positive read: he committed to the work when asked — 'in terms of if I'm committed to show up, yeah, I can commit myself' — engaged in detail with all three pillars and raised no objection to the method
Counter-evidence toward a negative read: he stated he is breaking even, declined to sell investments, and named a two-month horizon before he has financial room. Nothing changed that on this call.
outcome.next_step: Follow-up Zoom on Friday 3 July at 7:30pm UK time, same link, invite sent on the call. Prospect to work out what he can afford in the meantime.

notable.note: Two things a principal should see. First, this prospect disclosed a ruptured Achilles with three operations including an infection, permanent loss of ankle dorsiflexion, and a recent shoulder muscle tear treated with physiotherapy — and was then taken through a full presentation of loaded ballistic kettlebell training with no question about clinician clearance and an assurance that the coach would 'definitely address' the Achilles. Second, after the prospect disclosed he was breaking even and putting everything into a house renovation, the rep raised liquidating cryptocurrency to fund the programme and offered his own recent Solana sale as a model, continuing after the prospect said the market was down. The prospect declined. Set against that, the injury questioning and the sleep and nutrition questioning were the most thorough in this batch, and the money conversation was the most complete attempt at the scripted open-wallet sequence — with the permission question, the one move the manager had drilled him on two days earlier, omitted.

quality.notes: Persistent inversion. The very first line, 'Hello, Felipe', is attributed to Felipe Dublanc but is obviously the rep. Long stretches run under one label containing both voices — 00:02:22-00:02:30, 00:29:12-00:29:46 (which contains both the prospect's price reaction and the rep's isolate question), and 00:30:19-00:31:19. The pricing exchange around 00:29:12 is the worst affected passage and the GBP conversion inside it is not reliably reconstructable. Roles assigned from content throughout. There is also a brief video dropout at 00:10:26 after which the rep lost his own question — 'Oh, lost it. Dang it' — so one discovery question was asked and never completed.
